photoobj_star_cohort.name: photoobj_star_cohort
photoobj_star_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  p.extinction_r,
  pt.value AS photo_type_value,
  pt.name  AS photo_type_name
FROM photoobj p
LEFT JOIN photo_type pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
WHERE
  -- require a non-null clean flag (lifted literal)
  p.clean IS NOT NULL
  -- photometric type filter is NOT baked here; questions should add e.g. "AND p.type = <TYPE_VALUE>"
photoobj_star_cohort.description: Cohort of photoobj rows that represent a single detected object (one row per photoobj.objid). Intended to filter to objects by photometric type (e.g., STAR) and require non-null clean flag. Does not bake specific type literal; the type code equality is left to question_ops but exposes the joinable photo_type value->name.

photoobj_star_cohort_3.name: photoobj_star_cohort_3
photoobj_star_cohort_3.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.flags,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,
  p.cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.b,
  p.l,
  p.extinction_r,
  p.mjd,
  p.loadversion,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z
FROM photoobj AS p
JOIN photo_type AS pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
WHERE
  pt.name = 'STAR'
  AND p.clean IS NOT NULL
  AND p.clean <> 0
photoobj_star_cohort_3.description: Row-level cohort of photoobj rows that are flagged as STAR in the photo_type lookup and have non-null, non-zero clean flag. Keeps raw photometric and positional columns for selection and downstream filtering.

photoobj_basic_photometry.name: photoobj_basic_photometry
photoobj_basic_photometry.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  -- ensure flags/rowc/colc present even if source missing by selecting from best-available cohort
  COALESCE(s3.flags, p.flags) AS flags,
  COALESCE(s3.rowc, p.rowc) AS rowc,
  COALESCE(s3.colc, p.colc) AS colc,
  -- canonical cmodel mags: prefer photoobj_star_cohort_3 then photoobj_photometry_projection then photoobj table
  COALESCE(s3.cmodelmag_u, pp.cmodelmag_u, p.cmodelmag_u) AS cmodelmag_u,
  COALESCE(s3.cmodelmag_g, pp.cmodelmag_g, p.cmodelmag_g) AS cmodelmag_g,
  COALESCE(s3.cmodelmag_r, pp.cmodelmag_r, p.cmodelmag_r) AS cmodelmag_r,
  -- positional / projection fields: prefer cohort_3, then photometry_projection, then base photoobj
  COALESCE(s3.ra, pp.ra, p.ra) AS ra,
  COALESCE(s3.dec, pp.dec, p.dec) AS dec,
  -- galactic coordinates only available on cohort_3 or base photoobj
  COALESCE(s3.b, p.b) AS b,
  COALESCE(s3.l, p.l) AS l,
  COALESCE(s3.extinction_r, pp.extinction_r, p.extinction_r) AS extinction_r,
  -- mjd and loadversion: present in cohort_3 or photoobj
  COALESCE(s3.mjd, p.mjd) AS mjd,
  COALESCE(s3.loadversion, p.loadversion) AS loadversion,
  -- raw photometry: prefer cohort_3 then projection then base
  COALESCE(s3.u, pp.u, p.u) AS u,
  COALESCE(s3.g, pp.g, p.g) AS g,
  COALESCE(s3.r, pp.r, p.r) AS r,
  COALESCE(s3.i, pp.i, p.i) AS i,
  COALESCE(s3.z, pp.z, p.z) AS z
FROM photoobj AS p
-- photoobj_photometry_projection provides projected photometry/positions for many objects
LEFT JOIN photoobj_photometry_projection AS pp USING (objid)
-- photoobj_star_cohort_3 contains an extended set (flags, rowc, colc, b, l, mjd, loadversion)
LEFT JOIN photoobj_star_cohort_3 AS s3 USING (objid)
photoobj_basic_photometry.description: Canonicalized photoobj basic photometry and positional projection: ensures numeric photometry columns are exposed with consistent names and preserves raw values for u/g/r/i/z and cmodel magnitudes; intended for joins and downstream calculations (no filtering by type/clean).

specobj_linked_to_photoobj.name: specobj_linked_to_photoobj
specobj_linked_to_photoobj.body_sql:
SELECT

  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  s.z::real AS z,
  s.class::varchar AS class,
  s.mjd::integer AS mjd,
  s.plate::smallint AS plate,
  s.fiberid::smallint AS fiberid
FROM specobj s
specobj_linked_to_photoobj.description: One row per spectral observation (specobj) with linkage to its best matched photo object (bestobjid). Exposes spectral id, best photo obj id for joining, basic spectral metadata (z, class) to support existence/quality filters.

spectral_observations_alternative_lists.name: spectral_observations_alternative_lists

SELECT specobjid,
       'galspecline' AS source_list_name
FROM galspecline
UNION
SELECT specobjid,
       'spplines' AS source_list_name
FROM spplines
spectral_observations_alternative_lists.description: One row per spectroscopic object id listed in ancillary spectral lists (galspecline and spplines). Useful to include spectral observations referenced outside specobj.bestobjid linking.

photoobj_with_spec_assoc.name: photoobj_with_spec_assoc
photoobj_with_spec_assoc.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.type AS type,
  s.specobjid AS specobj_specobjid,
  s.bestobjid AS specobj_bestobjid,
  s.class AS specobj_class,
  s.z AS specobj_z,
  s.mjd AS specobj_mjd
FROM photoobj p
LEFT JOIN specobj s
  ON (s.bestobjid = p.objid OR s.specobjid = p.objid)
photoobj_with_spec_assoc.description: Photometric objects with flags indicating whether there exists an associated spectroscopic observation in specobj. Matches either via specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid or specobj.specobjid = photoobj.objid and exposes the matching specobj identifiers and basic spec metadata for downstream filters.

photoobj_canonical.name: photoobj_canonical
photoobj_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  p.run::smallint AS run,
  p.rerun::smallint AS rerun,
  p.field::smallint AS field,
  p.mode::smallint AS mode,
  p.type::smallint AS type,
  p.clean::integer AS clean,
  p.flags::bigint AS flags,
  p.ra::double precision AS ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS dec,
  p.u::real AS u,
  p.g::real AS g,
  p.r::real AS r,
  p.i::real AS i,
  p.z::real AS z
FROM
  photoobj AS p
WHERE
  -- lift question-specific literal: ensure one row per objid (photoobj.objid is primary key)
  p.objid IS NOT NULL
photoobj_canonical.description: Canonical, cleaned projection of the photoobj table exposing identifying keys, positional coordinates, photometric magnitudes and quality flags. Normalizes column names and keeps raw measures (no aggregation).
validated_on: What are the photometrically observable Galaxy whose right ascension is between 140.9 and 141.1, magnitude g is brighter than 18.0 and the difference of magitude u and magnitude g is greater than 2.2. Retrieve the objecti id, right ascension and declination of these objects.

photo_type_lookup_9.name: photo_type_lookup_9
photo_type_lookup_9.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.value AS value,

photo_type_lookup_9.description: Lookup table for photo object type codes with their human-readable name and description. Useful for joining type codes to names (e.g., to find 'galaxy' types).
validated_on: Show me object id, right ascensions and declinations of photometrically observed star in a certain area, of which the right ascension is between 185 and 186, declination is bertween 15 and 16.

photoobj_with_type.name: photoobj_with_type
photoobj_with_type.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.flags,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  pt.name AS type_name,
  pt.description AS type_description
FROM photoobj p
LEFT JOIN photo_type pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
photoobj_with_type.description: Denormalized join of photoobj to photo_type so each photometric detection includes its type name and description. Keeps one row per photoobj.objid.

specobj_spectral_classification.name: specobj_spectral_classification
specobj_spectral_classification.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid,
  s.bestobjid,
  s.class,
  s.subclass,
  s.ra,
  s.dec,
  s.z,
  s.mjd,
  s.plate,
  s.fiberid
FROM specobj AS s
specobj_spectral_classification.description: Spectroscopic object classifications and identifiers for linking to photometric objects. One row per spectroscopic observation (specobj).

photoobj_photometry_clean.name: photoobj_photometry_clean
photoobj_photometry_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  p.ra::double precision AS ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS dec,
  -- lift photometry null-replacement literals out: use NULL when value is NaN or exactly 0? here we normalize using NULL for very negative sentinel -9999 and NaN
  CASE WHEN p.u IS NOT NULL AND (p.u = 'NaN'::real OR p.u = -9999) THEN NULL ELSE p.u END AS u,
  CASE WHEN p.g IS NOT NULL AND (p.g = 'NaN'::real OR p.g = -9999) THEN NULL ELSE p.g END AS g,
  CASE WHEN p.r IS NOT NULL AND (p.r = 'NaN'::real OR p.r = -9999) THEN NULL ELSE p.r END AS r,
  CASE WHEN p.i IS NOT NULL AND (p.i = 'NaN'::real OR p.i = -9999) THEN NULL ELSE p.i END AS i,
  CASE WHEN p.z IS NOT NULL AND (p.z = 'NaN'::real OR p.z = -9999) THEN NULL ELSE p.z END AS z,
  -- normalize clean: treat NULL as 0 (not clean) only if explicitly desired; keep original clean value
  p.clean::integer AS clean,
  p.run::smallint AS run,
  p.rerun::smallint AS rerun,
  p.field::smallint AS field,
  p.type::smallint AS type,
  -- flags is optional in some upstreams; preserve as bigint
  p.flags::bigint AS flags
FROM
  photoobj p
photoobj_photometry_clean.description: Photometric measurements and basic quality flag (clean) for photo objects, normalized to consistent nulls. One row per photometric object (photoobj).

specobj_to_photoobj_linked.name: specobj_to_photoobj_linked
specobj_to_photoobj_linked.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid AS bestobjid,
  s.class AS spec_class,
  p.objid AS photo_objid,
  p.ra AS photo_ra,
  p.dec AS photo_dec,
  p.u AS u,
  p.g AS g,
  p.r AS r,
  p.i AS i,
  p.z AS z,
  p.clean AS clean
FROM specobj AS s
LEFT JOIN photoobj AS p
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
specobj_to_photoobj_linked.description: Denormalized join of spectroscopic classifications to their matched photometric objects using specobj.bestobjid -> photoobj.objid. One row per spectroscopic object (specobj).

specobj_to_photoobj_link.name: specobj_to_photoobj_link
specobj_to_photoobj_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid,
  s.bestobjid,
  s.ra,
  s.dec,
  s.z,
  s.class,
  s.scienceprimary,
  s.mjd
FROM specobj s
WHERE s.specobjid IS NOT NULL
  -- liftable literals for downstream filtering (example shown but not applied):
  -- 'min_z' = 0.0, 'max_z' = 1.0
specobj_to_photoobj_link.description: Denormalized links between spectral records and the photometric object ids they reference; one row per specobj.specobjid linking to bestobjid and basic spectroscopic flags and redshift fields for filtering match existence and quality.

photoobj_core.name: photoobj_core
photoobj_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.type,
  p.run,
  p.field,
  p.rerun,
  p.mode,
  p.clean
FROM
  -- prefer the cleaned star_cohort if available, else fall back to basic photometry projection
  (
    SELECT * FROM photoobj_star_cohort
  ) p
photoobj_core.description: Canonical cleaned/selected photometric object attributes needed for cross-match and spatial queries.

specobj_to_photoobj.name: specobj_to_photoobj
specobj_to_photoobj.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  s.mjd::integer AS mjd,
  s.plate::smallint AS plate,
  s.fiberid::smallint AS fiberid,
  s.ra::double precision AS ra,
  s.dec::double precision AS dec,
  s.z::real AS z,
  s.class::character varying AS class
FROM
  specobj s
specobj_to_photoobj.description: Mapping of spectroscopy records to their best-matched photometric object ids and basic spectroscopic attributes. Useful to identify which photometric objects have spectra.

photoobj_galaxy_with_spectrum_cohort.name: photoobj_galaxy_with_spectrum_cohort
photoobj_galaxy_with_spectrum_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra    AS ra,
  p.dec   AS dec,
  p.type  AS type,
  s.specobjid AS best_specobjid
FROM photoobj p
JOIN specobj s
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
WHERE p.type = '3'  -- galaxy type lifted as literal
  AND s.specobjid IS NOT NULL
photoobj_galaxy_with_spectrum_cohort.description: Cohort of photometric objects classified as galaxies that have an associated spectroscopy record (via specobj.bestobjid). Exposes photoobj identifiers and coordinates for downstream selection/aggregation.

photoobj_galaxy_cohort.name: photoobj_galaxy_cohort
photoobj_galaxy_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.type,
  p.clean
FROM
  photoobj AS p
JOIN
  photo_type AS pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
WHERE
  -- galaxy classification lifted literal: photo type name for galaxies is 'GALAXY'
  pt.name = 'GALAXY'
  -- must be marked clean/usable: clean = 1 (lifted literal)
  AND p.clean = 1

semantic_filters.type: galaxy (photoobj.type equals the photo_type value for galaxies)

photoobj_galaxy_cohort.description: Cohort view selecting photo-detected objects that are classified as galaxies and marked clean/usable. Useful as a reusable galaxy cohort for spatial, photometric and cross-match queries.

photoobj_neighbors_by_obj.name: photoobj_neighbors_by_obj
photoobj_neighbors_by_obj.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  n.neighborobjid AS neighborobjid,
  n.distance AS distance,
  n.type AS type,
  n.neighbortype AS neighbortype,
  n.mode AS mode,
  n.neighbormode AS neighbormode
FROM
  photoobj p
JOIN
  neighbors n
ON
  p.objid = n.objid
photoobj_neighbors_by_obj.description: Nearby-object relationships for each photoobj.objid including neighbor id and angular distance. One row per (objid, neighborobjid) pair — useful for isolation, blending, and neighbor-based quality filters.
counter_examples: Find the object ids, right ascensions and declinations of photometrically observable star whose right ascension is greater than 185, right ascension is less than 186, declination is greater than 15, declination is less than 16.

photoobj_star_rows.name: photoobj_star_rows
photoobj_star_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.type,
  p.clean
FROM photoobj AS p
JOIN photo_type_lookup AS pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
WHERE pt.name = 'STAR'
  AND p.clean <> 0
photoobj_star_rows.description: Row-level cohort of photoobj rows that represent stellar detections (photo type = STAR) and are marked clean (photometrically usable).

photoobj_with_type_name.name: photoobj_with_type_name
photoobj_with_type_name.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.type,
  pt.name AS type_name
FROM
  photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN
  photo_type AS pt
ON
  p.type = pt.value
photoobj_with_type_name.description: Denormalized photometric objects augmented with the photo_type.name so queries can filter by semantic type (e.g., 'STAR'). One row per photometric object.

spectroscopic_objects_basic.name: spectroscopic_objects_basic
spectroscopic_objects_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric                          AS specobjid,
  -- canonical best-match photometric object id for this spectrum (may be NULL)
  s.bestobjid::bigint                            AS bestobjid,
  -- primary spectroscopic coordinates (keep as double precision)
  s.ra::double precision                         AS ra,
  s.dec::double precision                        AS dec,
  -- spectroscopic classification string as recorded
  s.class::text                                  AS class,
  -- redshift from the spectroscopic pipeline
  s.z::real                                      AS z
FROM specobj s
-- keep one row per specobjid (specobj.specobjid is primary key)
spectroscopic_objects_basic.description: One-row-per spectroscopic observation with canonicalized key and primary coordinates and class; keep raw spectroscopic fields for joining/filtering.

specobj_classification.name: specobj_classification
specobj_classification.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid,
  s.bestobjid,
  s.class,
  s.z,
  s.zwarning,
  s.mjd,
  s.plate,
  s.fiberid
FROM specobj s
specobj_classification.description: Spectroscopic identification and redshift information per spectroscopic observation. Exposes mapping to best matched photo object (bestobjid), classification label, redshift and quality flags.

photoobj_specobj_join.name: photoobj_specobj_join
photoobj_specobj_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  p.ra::double precision AS ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS dec,
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  s.class::character varying AS class,
  s.z::real AS z,
  s.zwarning::integer AS zwarning
FROM
  photoobj p
JOIN
  specobj s
ON
  p.objid = s.bestobjid
photoobj_specobj_join.description: Denormalized view joining photo objects to their best spectroscopic observation (when available), exposing photo coordinates and spectroscopic class and redshift. One row per photo object that has a matching specobj.bestobjid.

specobj_core.name: specobj_core
specobj_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid,
  s.bestobjid,
  s.plateid,
  s.scienceprimary,
  s.segue2primary,
  s.survey,
  s.programname,
  /* lift mjd literal: prefer spectroscopic mjd from specobj; photometry mjd available elsewhere if needed */
  s.mjd,
  s.plate,
  s.fiberid,
  s.special_target1,
  s.segue2_target1,
  s.segue2_target2,
  s.ancillary_target1,
  s.ra,
  s.dec,
  s.z,
  s.zerr,
  s.zwarning,
  s.class,
  s.subclass,
  s.veldisp,
  s.veldisperr,
  s.loadversion
FROM specobj s
specobj_core.description: Canonical normalized spectroscopic object records exposing all specobj columns and canonical key fields; suitable as the base spectroscopic-row-level relation for filtering by position, redshift, class, and linking to photometry.

spectro_galaxy_indicators.name: spectro_galaxy_indicators
spectro_galaxy_indicators.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid,
  (g.specobjid IS NOT NULL) AS has_galspecline,
  (p.specobjid IS NOT NULL) AS has_spplines
FROM specobj AS s
LEFT JOIN galspecline AS g
  ON g.specobjid = s.specobjid
LEFT JOIN spplines AS p
  ON p.specobjid = s.specobjid
spectro_galaxy_indicators.description: Indicator rows linking spectroscopic objects to galaxy-specific derived/supplemental tables (galspecline and spplines). Offers boolean-like presence flags for each supplemental galaxy spectroscopic source to identify that the spectrum is recognized as a galaxy-spectrum by those pipelines.

spectroscopic_observations.name: spectroscopic_observations
spectroscopic_observations.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid,
  s.bestobjid,
  s.ra,
  s.dec,
  s.z,
  s.zerr,
  s.class,
  s.subclass,
  s.mjd,
  s.plate,
  s.fiberid
FROM specobj AS s
spectroscopic_observations.description: Mapping of spectroscopic observations to their best photometric object id and spectroscopic measurements; one row per specobj (spectroscopic observation).

photoobj_with_spec_link.name: photoobj_with_spec_link
photoobj_with_spec_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid AS bestobjid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  s.z AS z
FROM
  photoobj p
JOIN
  specobj s
    ON p.objid = s.bestobjid
photoobj_with_spec_link.description: Denormalized rows for photometric objects that have an associated spectroscopic observation; one row per photoobj.objid when linked to at least one specobj. Includes specobj key and redshift to enable spatial+spectroscopic queries.

photoobj_star_photometry.name: photoobj_star_photometry
photoobj_star_photometry.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  -- lift photometric values as literals outside view logic (no literals here; values come from source)
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,
  p.clean,
  -- ensure flags is present; if source doesn't provide flags, default to 0 (lifted literal)
  COALESCE(p.flags, 0) AS flags
FROM
  photoobj_star_cohort_3 p

semantic_filters.none: no intrinsic filters; keep all rows but normalize NULLs/types

photoobj_star_photometry.description: Canonical per-detection photometric measurements and positional columns for objects in photoobj, with cleaned numeric columns exposed for downstream filtering and color calculations.

photoobj_positional_index.name: photoobj_positional_index
photoobj_positional_index.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc
FROM photoobj p

semantic_filters.none: no intrinsic filters; includes rows even when some photometry is NULL

photoobj_positional_index.description: Subset/cohort view exposing basic positional and id columns for photoobj to support spatial joins or neighbor queries; one row per photo detection.

neighbors_pair_distances.name: neighbors_pair_distances
neighbors_pair_distances.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance,
  n.type,
  n.neighbortype,
  n.mode,
  n.neighbormode
FROM
  neighbors n

semantic_filters.none: no intrinsic filters; raw neighbor pairs retained

neighbors_pair_distances.description: Neighbor relations between photo detections: one row per neighbor pair (objid, neighborobjid) with distance and relation type fields from neighbors table.

photoobj_star_rows_32.name: photoobj_star_rows_32
photoobj_star_rows_32.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.ra,
  p.dec
FROM photoobj AS p
JOIN photo_type_lookup AS t
  ON p.type = t.value
WHERE
  -- classify as star according to the lookup name; lift literal
  t.name = 'STAR'
  -- require presence of basic positional/run identifiers and photometry
  AND p.objid IS NOT NULL
  AND p.run IS NOT NULL
  AND p.rerun IS NOT NULL
  AND p.field IS NOT NULL
  AND p.mode IS NOT NULL
  AND p.type IS NOT NULL
  AND p.ra IS NOT NULL
  AND p.dec IS NOT NULL
  AND p.u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.g IS NOT NULL
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.i IS NOT NULL
  AND p.z IS NOT NULL
photoobj_star_rows_32.description: All photoobj rows that are classified as stars (according to photo_type mapping) with non-null photometry and basic positional/run identifiers. This is a reusable star-cohort filter exposing raw magnitudes and identifying columns.

close_neighbor_pairs.name: close_neighbor_pairs
close_neighbor_pairs.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance,
  n.type,
  n.neighbortype,
  n.mode,
  n.neighbormode
FROM
  neighbors n
-- Lifted literals: none (view exposes raw neighbor relationships for arbitrary distance thresholds)
close_neighbor_pairs.description: Neighbor relationships between photo objects exposing pair identifiers and pairwise distance and role (objid, neighborobjid). Useful to find objects with nearby companions within arbitrary distance thresholds.

photoobj_with_close_neighbor.name: photoobj_with_close_neighbor
photoobj_with_close_neighbor.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance
FROM
  photoobj AS p
JOIN
  neighbors AS n
    ON p.objid = n.objid
photoobj_with_close_neighbor.description: Denormalized rows pairing a photoobj (one side of a neighbor relationship) with its neighbor's id and pair distance. One row per photoobj that participates in a neighbor relation (directed) with the neighbor's key and the pair distance; exposes photometry and neighbor metadata for easy filtering.

neighbors_pairs.name: neighbors_pairs
neighbors_pairs.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance,
  n.type,
  n.neighbortype,
  n.mode,
  n.neighbormode
FROM
  neighbors AS n
neighbors_pairs.description: Row-level neighbor pairs from the neighbors table exposing both members of the pair, the separation distance and type/mode flags. One row per neighbor relationship (as stored). Useful to filter by proximity and to join either side of a pair to photometry.

photoobj_with_type_name_36.name: photoobj_with_type_name_36
photoobj_with_type_name_36.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.r AS r,
  p.extinction_r AS extinction_r,
  p.type AS type,
  pt.name AS type_name
FROM photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN photo_type AS pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
photoobj_with_type_name_36.description: Denormalized per-photoobj row joining photoobj to photo_type to expose the human-readable type name for filtering and reporting.

photoobj_with_type_name_37.name: photoobj_with_type_name_37
photoobj_with_type_name_37.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.type,
  pt.name AS type_name,
  p.r,
  p.extinction_r,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.i,
  p.z
FROM photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN photo_type AS pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
photoobj_with_type_name_37.description: Denormalized per-photometric-object view that joins photoobj to photo_type to expose the type name alongside photometry and extinction for easy cohort selection by type name.

photoobj_with_type_name_38.name: photoobj_with_type_name_38
photoobj_with_type_name_38.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra    AS ra,
  p.dec   AS dec,
  p.u     AS u,
  p.g     AS g,
  p.r     AS r,
  p.i     AS i,
  p.z     AS z,
  p.type  AS type,
  t.name  AS name,
  p.clean AS clean,
  p.flags AS flags
FROM photoobj p
LEFT JOIN photo_type t
  ON p.type = t.value
photoobj_with_type_name_38.description: Denormalized per-photoobj row that includes the photo_type.name for each photoobj.type; useful for queries that filter by semantic type without manual lookup of integer codes.

photometry_core.name: photometry_core
photometry_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.run   AS run,
  p.rerun AS rerun,
  p.field AS field,
  p.mode  AS mode,
  p.type  AS type,
  p.clean AS clean,
  p.ra    AS ra,
  p.dec   AS dec,
  -- lift photometric band literals out if needed elsewhere; keep raw mags here
  p.u     AS u,
  p.g     AS g,
  p.r     AS r,
  p.i     AS i,
  p.z     AS z
FROM
  photoobj p
WHERE
  -- require positional and core magnitudes to be non-null
  p.ra IS NOT NULL
  AND p.dec IS NOT NULL
  AND p.u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.g IS NOT NULL
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.i IS NOT NULL
  AND p.z IS NOT NULL
photometry_core.description: Canonical per-detection photometric properties for objects in the photoobj table with non-null core magnitudes and positions. Normalizes field names and exposes raw magnitudes needed for color computations.

photoobj_galaxy_cohort_40.name: photoobj_galaxy_cohort_40
photoobj_galaxy_cohort_40.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z
FROM photoobj AS p
JOIN photo_type AS pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
WHERE
  -- lift literal: name for galaxy classification
  pt.name = 'GALAXY'
  -- ensure one row per objid (photoobj.objid is primary key)
photoobj_galaxy_cohort_40.description: Cohort of photoobj rows that represent photometric galaxies (rows where type corresponds to galaxy). This view isolates objects by photometric classification to be reused by queries needing galaxy-only photometry.

photoobj_colors.name: photoobj_colors
photoobj_colors.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  -- lift any question-specific literals out of the view: none required here
  -- computed adjacent colors: preserve NULL semantics (NULL if any operand NULL)
  (p.u - p.g) AS computed_color_u_minus_g,
  (p.g - p.r) AS computed_color_g_minus_r,
  (p.r - p.i) AS computed_color_r_minus_i,
  (p.i - p.z) AS computed_color_i_minus_z
FROM
  photoobj AS p
photoobj_colors.description: Per-photoobj projection that includes computed adjacent colors (u-g, g-r, r-i, i-z) alongside identifying columns; useful for color-selection cohorts and downstream filtering.

photoobj_star_photometry_rows.name: photoobj_star_photometry_rows
photoobj_star_photometry_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra    AS ra,
  p.dec   AS dec,
  p.u     AS u,
  p.g     AS g,
  p.r     AS r,
  p.i     AS i,
  p.z     AS z,
  p.type  AS type
FROM photoobj AS p
WHERE
  -- object must be classified as a star (lifted literal: star type value = 6)
  p.type = 6
  -- require non-null basic astrometry
  AND p.ra IS NOT NULL
  AND p.dec IS NOT NULL
  -- require non-null photometric magnitudes (keep rows with measured magnitudes)
  AND p.u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.g IS NOT NULL
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.i IS NOT NULL
  AND p.z IS NOT NULL
photoobj_star_photometry_rows.description: Row-level cohort of photoobj rows representing stellar objects (type indicates star) with non-null basic astrometry and photometric magnitudes. Keeps raw magnitude and position columns for downstream filtering and cuts.

photoobj_neighbors_distance.name: photoobj_neighbors_distance
photoobj_neighbors_distance.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance,
  n.type,
  n.neighbortype,
  n.mode,
  n.neighbormode
FROM
  photoobj AS p
JOIN
  neighbors AS n
    ON n.objid = p.objid
photoobj_neighbors_distance.description: Neighbors relation joined to photoobj objid to provide counts or nearest-neighbor distances per photoobj; exposes neighbor distances and neighbor ids to allow downstream deblending or isolation cuts (e.g. require no close neighbor within X arcsec).

photoobj_color_indices.name: photoobj_color_indices
photoobj_color_indices.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  -- color indices computed as (band1 - band2)
  -- lift any literal? none needed; use direct column differences
  (p.u - p.g) AS u_minus_g,
  (p.g - p.r) AS g_minus_r,
  (p.r - p.i) AS r_minus_i,
  (p.i - p.z) AS i_minus_z,
  -- has_all_mags is true when none of u,g,r,i,z are null
  (p.u IS NOT NULL AND p.g IS NOT NULL AND p.r IS NOT NULL AND p.i IS NOT NULL AND p.z IS NOT NULL) AS has_all_mags
FROM
  photoobj_photometry_projection p
photoobj_color_indices.description: Per-photoobj computed color indices and simple validity flags (no aggregation beyond one row per photoobj) to support color-based selections and downstream thresholds.

photoobj_sky_cohort.name: photoobj_sky_cohort
photoobj_sky_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  -- colour index u - g, lifted literal: if either mag is null result is null
  (p.u - p.g) AS u_minus_g
FROM
  photoobj_photometry_projection p
WHERE
  -- rectangular RA/Dec window lifted as literals (change these values outside the view if needed)
  p.ra BETWEEN 150.0 AND 160.0
  AND p.dec BETWEEN -1.0 AND 1.0
photoobj_sky_cohort.description: Cohort of photometric objects restricted to a rectangular RA/Dec window and exposing magnitudes and computed colour indices for quick spatial+colour filtering.

photoobj_basic_measurements.name: photoobj_basic_measurements
photoobj_basic_measurements.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  p.ra::double precision AS ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS dec,
  -- Provide 'g' as the best available calibrated PSF magnitude:
  -- prefer calibrated 'g' if present, else fall back to cmodelmag_g (less optimal),
  -- lift literals for missing-value sentinel
  CASE
    WHEN p.g IS NOT NULL THEN p.g
    WHEN p.cmodelmag_g IS NOT NULL THEN p.cmodelmag_g
    ELSE NULL
  END AS g
FROM photoobj_basic_photometry p
photoobj_basic_measurements.description: Canonical per-photometric-detection row with primary identifiers, sky position, band magnitudes, and quality flags normalized for querying.

specobj_classification_47.name: specobj_classification_47
specobj_classification_47.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  l.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  l.z::real AS z,
  l.class::varchar AS class
FROM specobj s
LEFT JOIN specobj_linked_to_photoobj l
  ON s.specobjid = l.specobjid
specobj_classification_47.description: Per-spectrum object row exposing spectroscopic identifiers, best matched photometric object id, redshift, and class/subclass for classification/filtering.

photoobj_with_spectrum.name: photoobj_with_spectrum
photoobj_with_spectrum.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.g AS g,
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.z AS z,
  s.class AS class
FROM
  photoobj p
LEFT JOIN
  specobj s
    ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
photoobj_with_spectrum.description: Denormalized view joining photoobj to its spectroscopic record (if any) via specobj.bestobjid, exposing both photometric properties and spectroscopic z/class for object-level cohort filtering.

spectroscopic_objects.name: spectroscopic_objects
spectroscopic_objects.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  s.class::text AS class,
  s.z::real AS z
FROM specobj AS s
spectroscopic_objects.description: One row per spectroscopic observation (specobj). Exposes spectroscopic identifiers, classification, redshift and linking key to photo objects (bestobjid and specobjid) for joining to photometry.

photo_objects_basic.name: photo_objects_basic
photo_objects_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.cmodelmag_g AS cmodelmag_g
FROM
  photoobj p

semantic_filters.cmodelmag_g IS NOT NULL: required for magnitude-based filters (exposed here as a canonical column presence requirement)

photo_objects_basic.description: One row per photo object (photoobj). Provides canonical position and basic photometric measures (cmodel magnitudes) and other identifiers useful for joins and filters. Null-cleaning and pass-through of raw mags; does not apply selection thresholds.

photo_to_specobj_linked.name: photo_to_specobj_linked
photo_to_specobj_linked.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid                          AS objid,
  p.ra                              AS ra,
  p.dec                             AS dec,
  p.cmodelmag_g                     AS cmodelmag_g,
  s.specobjid                       AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid                       AS bestobjid,
  s.class                           AS class,
  s.z                               AS z,
  -- link_type: 'bestobjid' when photo objid = specobj.bestobjid,
  --            'specobjid' when photo objid = specobj.specobjid,
  --            'both' if both match (unlikely but preserved)
  (CASE
     WHEN p.objid = s.bestobjid AND p.objid = s.specobjid THEN 'both'
     WHEN p.objid = s.bestobjid THEN 'bestobjid'
     WHEN p.objid = s.specobjid THEN 'specobjid'
     ELSE NULL
   END)                               AS link_type
FROM
  photoobj AS p
JOIN
  specobj AS s
  ON (p.objid = s.bestobjid OR p.objid = s.specobjid)
photo_to_specobj_linked.description: Denormalized mapping between photo objects and spectroscopic records: one row per photoobj linked to one specobj via either specobj.bestobjid or specobj.specobjid. Exposes both linking key used, the photo position/magnitude, and the spectroscopic class/redshift to support cohort filters without rejoining.
